properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 10 at 4:24PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
Atmospheric conditions are favorable for the development of funnel
clouds. These funnel clouds normally only protrude a few hundred
feet downward from the parent cloud, rotate or spin like a top,
and last a few minutes before dissipating.

These funnel clouds rarely touch the ground and typically do not
pose any sort of hazard. The atmospheric conditions that these
funnel clouds develop in do not support strong, damaging
tornadoes. However, on extremely rare occasions, these funnels can
briefly touch the ground and produce very minimal, if any, damage.

If threatening weather approaches, move indoors to a place of
safety. The National Weather Service will continue to closely
monitor the situation.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 10 at 3:17PM MDT until September 10 at 5:15PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 515 PM MDT.

* At 317 PM MDT, Emergency management reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding along US-70 near
Mescalero. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mescalero, Bent, Mud Canyon, South Tularosa Canyon, and Soldier
Canyon.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Tularosa Creek and Elk Canyon.
properties.instruction:
In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 5:15 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:15 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: Hardin, TX; Jefferson, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 10 at 2:57PM CDT until September 11 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Hardin and Jefferson
Counties.

For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pine Island Bayou near Sour Lake.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Water inundates roads in lowland areas near
the river. Low spots on Old Sour Lake Road are under water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 25.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 22.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:45 PM CDT Thursday was 25.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
evening and continue falling to 18.9 feet early Tuesday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 25.0
feet on 10/29/1975.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 300 AM CDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM THIS AFTERNOON TO FRIDAY MORNING

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 10 at 1:55PM MDT until September 10 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
* IMPACTS: Low humidities, unseasonably warm temperatures, and
gusty winds will create erratic fire behavior.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In South Central MT Fire Zones...123...124...127.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Central MT...Golden Valley...Musselshell...Wheatland.
In South Central MT...Park...Sweet Grass.
In Southwest MT...Gallatin.

* WIND: West 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 10 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: Mid to upper 80s.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS: The worst conditions are expected across
lower elevations that have received little precipitation in the
past week.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute
to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 10 at 2:07PM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
Atmospheric conditions are favorable for the development of funnel
clouds. These funnel clouds normally only protrude a few hundred
feet downward from the parent cloud, rotate or spin like a top,
and last a few minutes before dissipating.

These funnel clouds rarely touch the ground and typically do not
pose any sort of hazard. The atmospheric conditions that these
funnel clouds develop in do not support strong, damaging
tornadoes. However, on extremely rare occasions, these funnels can
briefly touch the ground and produce very minimal, if any, damage.

If threatening weather approaches, move indoors to a place of
safety. The National Weather Service will continue to closely
monitor the situation.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 10 at 1:52PM CDT until September 10 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING FOR
LOCATIONS IN NORTH DAKOTA SOUTH AND WEST OF THE MISSOURI RIVER AND
LAKE SAKAKAWEA...

.Warm and breezy conditions are expected over much of western and
parts of south central North Dakota today ahead of an approaching
cold front. Temperatures are forecast to climb into the upper 80s,
with afternoon humidity values as low as 13 percent. Winds this
afternoon are forecast to be southwest to west around 15 mph with
gusts to 30 mph. Due to the low humidity and breezy conditions with
abundant dry vegetation, critical fire weather conditions are
expected to continue into early this evening for locations in North
Dakota to the south and west of the Missouri River and Lake
Sakakawea.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of North Dakota south and west of the
Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea.

* TIMING...Until 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...Southwest to west around 15 mph with gusts to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity as low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity and warm temperatures can contribute to extreme
fire behavior.

NWSheadline: RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 10 at 1:41PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL
properties.description:
At 115 pm, the public reported reported a funnel cloud near Monmouth.

Atmospheric conditions exist that favor the possible formation
of weak circulations along a pre-existing boundary. Some of these
circulations are occurring underneath developing showers and
thunderstorms, where a funnel cloud may develop. Once the rain
begins, the funnel cloud usually dissipates.

Low hanging clouds can also appear to dip up and down at times,
but they will not show signs of any rapid rotation. An actual
funnel cloud will exhibit spinning in a counter-clockwise direction.

In rare instances these funnels may briefly touch down. Stay alert
and be prepared to move to a safe shelter if a funnel cloud
approaches the ground.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 10 at 11:23AM MST until September 10 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 105 to
110 expected. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Gila Bend, Sonoran Desert Natl Monument, Tonopah Desert,
Gila River Valley, Kofa, and Southeast Yuma County.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water, and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 10 at 10:17AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Alafia River At Lithia affecting Hillsborough County.

Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 affecting DeSoto County.

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Florida...

Little Manatee River At Wimauma at US 301 affecting Hillsborough
County.

Manatee River Near Myakka Head at SR 64 affecting Manatee County.

.Rising water levels are expected over the next several days along
the Alafia River At Lithia and Horse Creek Near Arcadia at SR 72 due
to recent heavy rainfall. The Little Manatee River At Wimauma at US
301 and Manatee River Near Myakka Head at SR 64 are no longer
forecast to reach Minor Flood Stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Horse Creek near Arcadia at SR 72.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The access road to Hidden Oak is
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 7.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Sunday morning and continue rising to 12.1 feet Sunday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.1
feet on 09/30/2003.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this morning at 1130 AM EDT.

properties.description:
The combination of hot temperatures and elevated humidity levels
will produce heat index values between 108 and 111 degrees for
several hours this afternoon into this evening. A few locations
may briefly experience heat index values above 111 degrees.

light weight and light colored clothing and take frequent breaks
from the heat. Young children and pets should never be left
unattended in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Kings (Brooklyn); Southwest Suffolk; Southeast Suffolk; Southern Queens; Southern Nassau
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 10 at 2:58AM EDT until September 10 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents, with 3 to 6 ft breaking surf.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* RIP CURRENT IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely
for all people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the
beaches should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep
even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* BEACH IMPACTS...Minor beach flooding is possible during the
times of high tide today, particularly this morning.
properties.instruction:
If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

* High water flowing down the Kuskokwim River, in combination with
storm surge pushing up the up river, could cause water levels to
rise between bankfull and minor flood stage.
* The highest water levels would occur if the downstream high water
flow, storm surge, and high tide all occurred simultaneously.

Potential Impacts:
* More likely scenario: Bankfull conditions with no flooding
expected.
* Worst case scenario: Nuisance flooding in low-lying areas.

Locations:
* Along Kuskokwim River, from Bethel south to Napakiak.
* Along Johnson River, from Nunapitchuk and Kasigluk south to the
Kuskokwim River.

Timing:
* Highest water levels will likely occur around high tide on Friday,
from about 11 AM through 4 PM.
* Strongest winds (south to southwesterly, gusting up to 30 to 45
mph) from about 4 PM Thursday through 4 PM Friday.

Next Steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 9 at 3:46PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

For communities along Kuskokwim River (Tuntutuliak):
* High water flowing down the Kuskokwim River, in combination with
storm surge flowing up river, could cause water levels to increase
as high as bankfull to minor flood stage during high tide.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide, which will
be from around 11 AM through 4 PM.

For communities along the coast (Kongiganak, Kwigillingok, Kipnuk,
Toksook Bay, Tununak):
* Strong onshore winds could bring the potential for coastal erosion
and minor coastal flooding in the worst case scenario. The more
likely scenario is that water levels will remain below 1 to 2 feet
above the normal highest tide, and no flooding will occur.
* Timing: Water levels will be highest during high tide on Friday,
from about 10 AM through 2 PM. Communities further north, like
Toksook Bay and Tununak, may see higher water levels during
Thursday's high tide as well.

Next steps:
* Monitor the forecast for updates.
* Be prepared to take action in case of minor flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Noatak Valley; Lower Kobuk Valley; Upper Kobuk Valleys
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 9 at 1:51PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Streams draining southern slopes of the Western Brooks Range.

Incoming rainfall from a atmospheric river will bring rainfall to the
southern slopes of the western end of the Brooks Range through
Friday.  Rainfall totals may exceed two inches in some locations and
cause significant rises on small streams.

The Kobuk, Noatak, and Wulik Rivers should also see rises from this
system into the weekend, but no flooding is expected.

NWSheadline: HYDROLOGIC OUTLOOK IN EFFECT THROUGH FRIDAY AFTERNOON FOR RAINFALL IN THE KOBUK, NOATAK, AND WULIK RIVER VALLEYS

Warning.

burning is not recommended.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 9 at 3:14AM PDT until September 10 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures 10 to 20 degrees above
normal during the day, with overnight lows also running 10 to 20
degrees above normal.

* WHERE...Bay Area and Central Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration. Impacts possible in some health systems and in
heat-sensitive industries. Hot conditions can cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

NWSheadline: HEAT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM PDT THURSDAY
